problems.stem: What is the defining architectural strength of swarm intelligence?
options: Every agent waits for a central commander before acting
Useful global behavior can emerge from simple local rules
The system works only when every agent has full information
A queen node is always required for control
problems.explanation: Swarm systems rely on local interaction rules that scale into coordinated collective behavior.

options: Direct voice communication between every pair of agents
Indirect coordination through changes in the environment
A centralized scheduling algorithm run by one master node
A method for forcing all agents into one exact path
problems.explanation: Stigmergy describes coordination mediated by environmental traces such as pheromone-like markers or other shared signals.

problems.stem: In Reynolds-style flocking logic, which set best captures the classic local rules?
options: Separation, alignment, and cohesion
Compression, combustion, and rotation
Navigation, taxation, and encryption
Authority, punishment, and hierarchy
problems.explanation: The classic boids model is built around separation, alignment, and cohesion.

problems.stem: Why might engineers choose many cheap robots over one powerful centralized robot in a disaster zone?
options: Because distributed systems can remain functional even when many units fail
Because swarms require no sensing at all
Because centralized systems are always impossible to build
Because local rules prevent any communication between robots
problems.explanation: Distributed swarms can be more robust because failure of some units does not collapse the whole mission.

problems.stem: What is the best example of analogical transfer from swarm biology into engineering?
options: Painting robots to look like ants so they appear coordinated
Translating local signaling and task allocation principles into distributed control rules
Forcing one controller to issue every motion command while calling the system a swarm
Copying insect body shape even when the task is warehouse routing
problems.explanation: The engineering value comes from abstracting principles such as local signaling, redundancy, and distributed task allocation, not from copying biological appearance.

problems.stem: Which move best avoids fixation during biologically inspired ideation?
options: Lock onto the first organism that seems relevant and keep its form throughout development
Compare multiple biological strategies and restate each as functions, rules, and constraints
Use only one biological analogy so the team stays consistent
Reject engineering metrics until after a biological form is chosen
problems.explanation: Fixation drops when teams compare several analogies and translate them into functions and constraints instead of overcommitting to one literal source.
